Subject: Hosted API security questionnaire — residency & retention

Hi Olga,

Thanks for agreeing to take our hosted-API section of the security questionnaire. We have a couple of scoped questions focused solely on data residency and deletion timelines (we're at the legal review stage). The items below are the ones our privacy team needs confirmed for the contract:

1) Where does customer request payload and model context reside (region-level)? Do you support region pinning per tenant?
2) What is the retention for non-PHI request logs, prompt/response content, and diagnostics? Please give short and long retention windows and indicate backups/snapshots retention.
3) If BlueParrot requests a full erasure for a tenant, what are the stepwise timelines (active store deletion, backup scrub, third-party snapshots)?
4) Does KV/prefix caching used by the runtime persist to disk or inside ephemeral memory only?
5) Any evidence we can point our auditors to (diagram, matrix, or playbook)?

We attached the RFI template — I can take your answers directly in a csv or pdf. Rough timeline: we need a completed reply by end of day Monday (12/11).

Best,

Eleanor —

Thanks for the clear list. Below are concise answers we maintain for hosted customers; I kept each item numbered to match your template. I'm attaching a residency matrix and a csv exported with the same rows in case you prefer copy/paste into your RFI doc.

1) Residency / region pinning: request payload, transient model context, and operational metadata are stored in the regional tenant shard you select at onboarding. We support explicit region pinning per tenant for our hosted product (US, EU, APAC as separate deployments). Persistent storage (logs, audit trails) remain in the pinned region unless you request multi-region replication (enterprise-only add-on).

2) Retention windows (typical hosted defaults):
   - Short-term request metadata (timestamps, routing headers): 30 days.
   - Prompt & response content (unredacted customer-sent prompts + model outputs): retained by default 90 days for debugging and quality monitoring. Can be configured to 30 days or disabled at tenant level.
   - Diagnostics & enriched logs (stack traces, performance traces): 90 days.
   - Aggregated/anonymized usage telemetry: retained 365 days.

   Backups & snapshots: automated daily snapshots are kept up to 30 days in the same region by default. Point-in-time backups are retained for up to 90 days for customers on our enhanced retention plan (documented in the matrix).

3) Erasure timelines (customer-initiated full tenant wipe):
   - Active store deletion: 24 hours to remove tenant records from live stores (after authorization + ticket open).
   - Cache invalidation: prefix/KV caches are invalidated immediately on wipe.
   - Background deletes & index rebuild: within 72 hours most pointers are removed; dependent indexes may take up to 7 days to fully reconcile under heavy load.
   - Backup & snapshot scrub: backups are scrubbed on their normal retention cycle; we trigger expedited scrub with a 30-day maximum window for hosted customers requesting expedited erasure.
   - Third-party snapshots (cloud provider snapshots, if any): treated per provider contract; we assist and coordinate — typical maximum 30 days for coordination + verification.

   Note: we provide an erasure confirmation report (timestamped) once the active store and cache invalidation steps are complete; final scrub verification follows once backups are confirmed removed.

4) KV / prefix caching: the runtime uses in-memory KV caches pinned to serving instances. We do not persist the KV cache to durable disk for hosted tenants. Cache shards are ephemeral and tied to instance lifecycle; on instance termination the KV cache is discarded. We also have TTLs per key and can proactively flush caches for a tenant on request.

5) Evidence: attached residency matrix (PDF) and the csv (same rows). Additional artifacts we can provide on request: architecture diagram showing regional isolation, SOC2 audit excerpt for data-handling controls, and an example erasure confirmation report.

Attachments: redwood_hostedapi_residency_matrix_2028.pdf, bp-rfi-answers-20281209.csv

I'll follow up with a short note that expands on backups and snapshots to make sure you have language for your contract.

—Olga

A) For the prompt/response content retained 90 days by default — if we opt to reduce to 30 days, can you confirm there are no archival copies outside the region (e.g., for analytics pipelines)?
B) For expedited backup scrub (30 days max) — can you confirm the process: is this initiated by Redwood or by BlueParrot and do you provide a signed acknowledgement once scrub completes?
C) For KV cache — can you provide a short statement we can include in the contract that the cache is ephemeral and not persisted to disk?

If we can get short, contract-ready bullets for A–C that would be hugely helpful. We can accept them inline in the csv or as a short signed statement.

Eleanor — short contract bullets below (feel free to copy verbatim):

A) Regional archival: "When a tenant elects region pinning, all customer prompt/response content and associated backups remain stored in the selected region. Redwood does not replicate or archive customer prompt/response content to other regions for analytics or operational purposes unless explicitly enabled via a documented multi-region replication add-on requested by the customer."

B) Expedited backup scrub: "Expedited backup scrub is available for hosted customers via a written request to Redwood's Security & Ops team. Upon customer authorization, Redwood initiates a scrub and will provide a signed Erasure Completion Statement reporting the actions taken and timestamps. Standard maximum window for completing the expedited scrub is 30 calendar days (this includes coordination with cloud provider snapshot timelines)."

C) KV cache statement: "Redwood's hosted serving runtime maintains KV/prefix caches in memory only; caches are not persisted to disk. Cache contents are ephemeral, tied to serving instance lifecycles, and are flushed immediately upon tenant erasure requests or instance termination."

I've added these three bullets to the csv and re-attached the artifacts. If you want a short PDF signed by our Head of Security, we can generate that next business day.
